title: MathCamp 2026
text:
Welcome
This is the interactive companion book for MathCamp 2026, the math camp for the incoming Political Science PhD cohort. It replaces last year’s slide-based sessions (archived in Resources/Slide Decks 2025/) with interactive, web-based material built in Quarto.

title: MathCamp 2026
text:
How to use this book
Each session is its own chapter with two sub-chapters:

Slides — the in-class slideshow (also browsable on its own at slides/index.html).
Programming Lecture — a webpage walking through the same material with runnable R code, worked examples, and (eventually) interactive visualizations via plotly, Shiny, or similar R tooling.

2.0.1 R and R Studio
Use the link here to install RStudio on your systems.






NoteThe connection between R and R Studio



R is a programming language while RStudio, an integrated development environment (IDE), provides the interface for us to run computations. You can think of R as the engine of the car, and RStudio as the dashboard.




2.0.2 Zotero
Zotero is a reference management tool. It allows you to maintain a structured bibliography. Its integration with various web browsers and software like MS Word and R, makes it a fantastic tool for keeping track of readings as well as citing them.

title: 4  Programming Lecture
text:
4.0.1 Simulating a random process: coin flips


Code
set.seed(2026)
flips <- sample(c("H", "T"), size = 10000, replace = TRUE)
table(flips) / length(flips)


flips
    H     T 
0.499 0.501 




4.0.2 The Monty Hall problem, by simulation


Code
monty_hall <- function(switch = TRUE) {
  doors <- 1:3
  car <- sample(doors, 1)
  pick <- sample(doors, 1)
  reveal <- sample(setdiff(doors, c(car, pick)), 1)
  final <- if (switch) setdiff(doors, c(pick, reveal)) else pick
  final == car
}

set.seed(2026)
n <- 5000
p_switch <- mean(replicate(n, monty_hall(switch = TRUE)))


Warning in mean.default(replicate(n, monty_hall(switch = TRUE))): argument is
not numeric or logical: returning NA


Code
p_stay <- mean(replicate(n, monty_hall(switch = FALSE)))
data.frame(strategy = c("switch", "stay"), win_rate = c(p_switch, p_stay))


  strategy win_rate
1   switch       NA
2     stay    0.347




4.0.3 Combinations: the birthday problem


Code
birthday_prob <- function(n_people) 1 - exp(lchoose(365, n_people) + lfactorial(n_people) - n_people * log(365))
sapply(c(10, 23, 50), birthday_prob)


[1] 0.1169482 0.5072972 0.9703736

title: 6  Programming Lecture
text:
6.0.1 Numerical differentiation: the secant approaching the tangent


Code
f <- function(x) x^3 - 2 * x
secant_slope <- function(f, x, h) (f(x + h) - f(x)) / h

x0 <- 1
hs <- 10^-(1:6)
data.frame(h = hs, secant_slope = secant_slope(f, x0, hs))


      h secant_slope
1 1e-01     1.310000
2 1e-02     1.030100
3 1e-03     1.003001
4 1e-04     1.000300
5 1e-05     1.000030
6 1e-06     1.000003




Code
# Analytic derivative f'(x) = 3x^2 - 2, so f'(1) = 1
f_prime <- function(x) 3 * x^2 - 2
f_prime(1)


[1] 1




6.0.2 Differentiation rules by symbolic differentiation


Code
D(expression(x^3 - 2 * x), "x")


3 * x^2 - 2


Code
D(expression(sin(x) * x^2), "x") # product rule


cos(x) * x^2 + sin(x) * (2 * x)




6.0.3 Optimization: finding an extremum


Code
g <- function(x) (x - 2)^2 + 1
result <- optimize(g, interval = c(-10, 10))
result


$minimum
[1] 2

$objective
[1] 1




Code
curve(g, from = -2, to = 6, lwd = 2, main = "g(x) = (x - 2)^2 + 1")
points(result$minimum, result$objective, col = "red", pch = 19)

title: 8  Programming Lecture
text:
8.0.1 Area under the curve, numerically


Code
f <- function(x) x^2
result <- integrate(f, lower = 0, upper = 3)
result


9 with absolute error < 1e-13




Code
# Analytic check: integral of x^2 from 0 to 3 is x^3/3 -> 9
curve(f, from = -0.5, to = 3.5, lwd = 2, main = "Area under f(x) = x^2, [0, 3]")
xs <- seq(0, 3, length.out = 200)
polygon(c(xs, rev(xs)), c(f(xs), rep(0, length(xs))), col = rgb(0, 0, 1, 0.2), border = NA)











8.0.2 Reversing differentiation: symbolic antiderivative check


Code
# f(x) = x^2, F(x) = x^3/3 + C; verify F' = f
F <- function(x) x^3 / 3
h <- 1e-6
x0 <- 2
(F(x0 + h) - F(x0 - h)) / (2 * h) # numerical derivative of F at x0


[1] 4


Code
f(x0)


[1] 4




8.0.3 Multivariate calculus: partial derivatives and the gradient


Code
f2 <- function(x, y) x^2 * y + y^3

partial_x <- function(x, y, h = 1e-6) (f2(x + h, y) - f2(x - h, y)) / (2 * h)
partial_y <- function(x, y, h = 1e-6) (f2(x, y + h) - f2(x, y - h)) / (2 * h)

gradient <- c(partial_x(1, 2), partial_y(1, 2))
gradient


[1]  4 13




8.0.4 Application: deriving OLS with lm()


Code
set.seed(2026)
x <- rnorm(100)
y <- 2 + 3 * x + rnorm(100, sd = 0.5)

fit <- lm(y ~ x)
coef(fit) # OLS solves the same minimization problem worked out by hand in the slides


(Intercept)           x 
   2.057986    2.971808
